posts.angle: Show the two separate jobs in an existing doorway routine
posts.headline: A muddy-paw station has two jobs—and one stop rule
posts.copy: Heavy mud may need warm—not hot—water. The water then needs a towel. A size-qualified MudBuster and one pocketed shammy make sense only for a familiar routine: never force the paw, and stop for pain, injury, guarding, panic, or resistance.
posts.assetBrief: Original vertical threshold diagram with a generic water-filled paw cup on the dirty side, a pocketed towel on a hook, warm-water symbol, stop-hand symbol, and four paw icons moving toward the clean side; no product photography, logos, or handling demonstration.
posts.altText: Diagram showing a familiar muddy-paw routine with a warm-water rinse, pocketed towel, and a stop symbol for dog discomfort or resistance.

posts.angle: Show the published MudBuster ranges and preserve the manufacturer’s sizing gap
posts.headline: A paw over 2 but under 2.5 inches has no published MudBuster size
posts.copy: Dexas lists small for paws up to 2 inches, medium from 2.5 to 3.5 inches, and large above 3.5 inches. If the paw is over 2 but under 2.5 inches, ask Dexas or skip the cup. Retailer reviews cannot fill the gap.
posts.assetBrief: Five original illustrated slides: published small range, published medium range, published large range, highlighted over-2-to-under-2.5-inch gap, and ask-maker-or-skip card; no invented measuring method, logos, product photos, or simulated fit.
posts.altText: Carousel showing Dexas published paw-width ranges and the unresolved gap between over 2 inches and under 2.5 inches.

posts.angle: Make bottle compatibility the portable-rinse gift check
posts.headline: A travel dog shower needs a tested bottle and a comfortable dog
posts.copy: The Kurgo attachment is designed for standard threaded PET bottles, but buyer reports show that not every bottle works the same. Test the exact bottle, use warm—not hot—water on stable footing, never force paw handling, and pack one pocketed towel.
posts.assetBrief: Five original illustrated slides: generic shower attachment, two bottle-thread silhouettes, warm-water and non-slip symbols, no-force stop card, and a pocketed towel; no product photography, logos, or handling demonstration.
posts.altText: Carousel showing a bottle-thread check, warm-water rinse, non-slip surface, stop-for-resistance rule, and pocketed towel.

posts.angle: Choose one drying towel by the specific job: hand pockets or wringing
posts.headline: Does the gift need hand pockets—or one towel they can wring out?
posts.copy: The Soggy Doggy gives the person two hand pockets for targeted paw drying. The 17-by-27-inch Absorber is a flat PVA towel that can be wrung and reused, but it has no pockets, cannot go in a dryer, and needs its own storage routine. Pick one observed advantage; do not buy both by default.
posts.assetBrief: Original two-column decision card labeled Hand pockets and Wring and reuse, with generic towel silhouettes, laundry symbols, one hook or tube-storage icon, and a single-choice reminder; no product photography or logos.
posts.altText: Decision card comparing a compact pocketed towel with a flat wringable towel and their different care needs.

posts.angle: Turn stable footing into a visible pre-gift check
posts.headline: A backing claim is not a promise on every floor
posts.copy: Show the door swing, measured standing spot, and flatness and movement check on the actual surface. Keep the dog on a dry non-slip area, and end with the washer-space and hang-dry check. One compensated-platform owner account is only subjective experience, not proof of stability.
posts.assetBrief: Original unbranded storyboard with a doorway plan, door-swing arc, generic mat, flat-edge close-up, movement arrows crossed out, washer icon, drying hook, and subjective-evidence label; no simulated product test.
posts.altText: Short video storyboard checking a muddy-paw mat for door clearance, flat edges, movement, washer fit, drying space, and evidence limits.

posts.angle: Make the no-purchase answer part of the gift advice
posts.headline: Sometimes the old towel is already the right answer
posts.copy: If a bowl and washable towel already handle the muddy-door routine, keep them. Add one specialty item only for a named problem, and only when the dog is comfortable with the handling. Never force a new paw-washing routine for the sake of a gift.
posts.assetBrief: Original vertical checklist labeled Keep, Replace one, and Pair, using a generic bowl, towel, pocketed shammy, paw cup, and mat; no product photography or logos.
posts.altText: Checklist showing when to keep an existing bowl and towel, replace one tool, or pair a rinse tool with a drying towel.
